key_insight: Extending cuDOLFINx to assemble mixed-dimensional interface problems enables end-to-end GPU execution of the cardiac EMI model while preserving high-level FEniCS programming.
engineering_relevance: The implementation accelerates finite element models with volumetric regions coupled through lower-dimensional interfaces and can support applications beyond cardiac modeling.
method: Add GPU assembly for mixed-dimensional interface coupling in cuDOLFINx.
Combine assembly with GPU-resident Krylov solvers and algebraic multigrid preconditioning.
Benchmark CPU and multi-GPU execution on regular and realistic 3D cardiac geometries.
evidence_signal: Strong and weak scaling tests reached 8000 cells and 22 million degrees of freedom; one GH200 node delivered assembly performance comparable to roughly two to three 144-core CPU nodes, depending on scaling regime and geometry.
watch_item: Solver speedups depend on geometry, preconditioning, and scale; GPU advantages on regular geometries emerged mainly for larger problems and node counts.
paper_title: Multi-GPU Acceleration of Interface Problems in FEniCS, with Application to Cardiac Modeling
